LESSON: COUNTING CONCRETE OBJECTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 2.3: Counting concrete objects
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Counting concrete objects, part of NUMBERS in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How many objects are these? 2. How many learners are in your group? 3. How many boys or girls are in your group? 4. Why do we match objects?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. count concrete objects 1-9 used by family members for development of numeracy skills,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Counting concrete objects in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. demonstrate one to one correspondence of number symbols (1-9) and a group of concrete objects used by family member,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Counting concrete objects in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy counting concrete objects used by family members,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Counting concrete objects in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Counting concrete objects together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: Speaking. The learner speaks clearly and effectively while talking to and listening to each

other as they count concrete objects accurately and match to the corresponding numerals in groups or pairs.

Values:
• Unity: The learner works together harmoniously in groups or in pairs to complete the task of matching concrete objects to

numerals

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Safety: The learners observe safety while manipulating and demonstrating correspondence of number symbols with concrete

objects.

Link to other activity areas:

• Creative Activities: The learner sings and dances songs involving counting of concrete objects used by family members.

• Environmental Activities: Family concept in environmental activities is reinforced as the learner counts concrete objects used by

family members.

Suggested Resources:

Plates, spoons, cups/mugs, sufuria, jugs, dishes, basins
